name: agentkcal
description: Show a compact summary of locally recorded AI agent tokens and illustrative Wh/kcal when the user asks about AI usage, energy or calories. Refresh local logs only when requested.
---

Use the connected AgentKcal MCP server's `get_usage` tool. Default to today's UTC usage. Honor the user's agent, period, session and language; supported language codes are `en`, `ru`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `ja` and `pt-BR`. Use the user's language, with English as the fallback. Do not guess the active session ID or call other tools to search conversation logs.

If the user explicitly asks for current or refreshed usage, first call `sync_usage`, optionally selecting a supported adapter. Mention any error/warning counts. Cursor, OpenCode and Cline require user-configured export or task-journal paths; do not discover their private databases or credentials.

Return one compact line with the period, tokens, approximate Wh and kcal. State that it uses the local ledger and include `last_event_at` when freshness matters. These are energy scenarios, not measured power, money, food consumed or human calories burned. The current tool invocation itself may not yet be present in the agent's log.

If MCP is unavailable and the installed `agentkcal` executable is on PATH, run `agentkcal status --language CODE` with the user's supported language code using the host's normal shell tool. Add `--sync` only for an explicit refresh request. Never install packages or alter agent settings automatically.

Offer the local dashboard only if the user requests history or detailed comparisons. Never claim that this skill installs a persistent footer or editor status bar.

AgentKcal

Your AI agents, in tokens, watt-hours, and a little perspective.

AgentKcal brings usage from AI coding agents into one local ledger. See consumed tokens, explore configurable energy estimates in watt-hours and kilocalories, and compare that energy with familiar foods. Use the CLI or an in-agent summary during everyday work, then open the dashboard for history and comparisons. Records stay in a local SQLite database; AgentKcal makes no outbound network requests. **Energy values are estimates based on configurable assumptions, not power measurements.** Kilocalories express equivalent physical energy, not food consumed or calories burned. [How estimates work](docs/methodology.md). [![AgentKcal dashboard with synthetic usage, energy estimates, food comparisons and agent history](docs/images/dashboard.png)](docs/images/dashboard.png) _Dashboard in light mode with synthetic demo data. Open the image to view the full-resolution screenshot._ ## Quick start Requires **Node.js 24.12+** and npm. ```sh git clone https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal.git cd AgentKcal npm ci npm run build npm run demo ``` Open **http://127.0.0.1:8765**. The demo uses a temporary database, does not read your agent logs, and removes its data when stopped normally. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop the server. A prebuilt CLI archive and SHA-256 checksum are available in [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal/releases). [Version history](CHANGELOG.md). The examples below run directly from the repository. You can also [install the CLI from a package](docs/cli.md#install-the-cli). ## Track your usage ```sh # Create configuration and inspect available adapters. node dist/cli.js init node dist/cli.js agents # Import local logs and show today's UTC usage. node dist/cli.js sync node dist/cli.js status # View a longer period or open the dashboard. node dist/cli.js summary --days 30 node dist/cli.js serve ``` Imports can be repeated: unchanged events are skipped and updated snapshots replace existing records. Dashboard sync runs the same import as the CLI. Refreshing the page alone reads the ledger without importing logs. For agents that use exports or explicitly selected task journals: ```sh node dist/cli.js sync --adapter cursor --path ./cursor-usage.csv node dist/cli.js sync --adapter opencode --path ./session-export.json node dist/cli.js sync --adapter cline --path /path/to/tasks ``` For an isolated example that does not use your existing ledger: ```sh node dist/cli.js --data-dir ./local-data sync --adapter generic --path examples/usage.jsonl node dist/cli.js --data-dir ./local-data summary --days 0 ``` See the [CLI reference](docs/cli.md) for filtering, export formats, exit codes and all commands. ## Supported agents - **Claude Code:** local project JSONL, including nested subagent journals. Honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. - **Codex:** local rollout JSONL from sessions and archived sessions. Honors `CODEX_HOME`. - **Gemini CLI:** local session JSON and JSONL under `~/.gemini/tmp/`. - **Cursor:** Usage CSV exports with the required token columns. - **OpenCode:** session JSON exports in classic or flat message format. - **Cline:** explicitly selected `ui_messages.json` task journals. - **Other agents:** normalized JSONL through the `generic` adapter, or a dedicated TypeScript adapter. Support depends on the source format and the availability of usage counters. Connecting an agent to MCP does not add missing telemetry. [Formats, default paths and accounting rules](docs/adapters.md). ## See usage inside your agent ```sh node dist/cli.js status --agent codex --sync --language en node dist/cli.js integration --agent claude --language en node dist/cli.js integration --agent codex ``` - **Claude Code:** a native, persistent status line shows the current session's tokens and approximate Wh/kcal without invoking a model. - **Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode and Cline:** a local stdio MCP server provides compact summaries on demand inside the conversation. Skills and command templates make the tools easier to invoke. The `integration` command prints settings to merge into your agent's configuration. It does not change that configuration. MCP separates `get_usage` from `sync_usage`, so reading a summary does not silently import logs. MCP summaries enter the agent's context and may be sent to its model provider. Your underlying ledger remains local. [Set up an integration](docs/integrations.md). ## Languages, themes and food comparisons The dashboard and compact summaries support **English, Russian, Spanish, German, French, Japanese and Brazilian Portuguese**. Language codes: `en`, `ru`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `ja`, `pt-BR`. The first visit uses a supported browser language; you can change it in the top bar. Numbers, dates and portion labels follow the selected locale. Agent/model IDs, custom scenario labels, source diagnostics and export field names retain their original form. General CLI help and full text reports are in English. Choose **System**, **Light** or **Dark**. System follows live OS theme changes. Language, theme and the selected food are saved in browser localStorage and shared between tabs at the same local address. The food panel compares estimated kcal with **buckwheat, dumplings, bread, milk, bananas, rice, corn or potatoes**. Each product states its assumed portion and energy value. Five illustrations show whole or partial portions; a badge counts additional portions. The progress bar shows the fraction of the next portion. These are energy comparisons, not a dietary target or a record of food consumed. [Portions, formulas and sources](docs/methodology.md#food-comparisons). ## Estimates and accuracy Adapters normalize usage into disjoint token buckets: ```text input + output + cache_read + cache_write + reasoning = total_tokens ``` The default token scenario uses configurable Wh-per-million coefficients and a data-center overhead factor, PUE: ```text Wh = PUE × Σ(bucket_tokens × bucket_Wh_per_million / 1,000,000) kcal = Wh × 3,600 / 4,184 ``` The initial coefficients are **100 input, 400 output, 10 cache read, 125 cache write and 400 reasoning**, with **PUE 1.2**. They are illustrative assumptions shared across models, not vendor efficiency benchmarks. When paired GPU time and power are supplied, `PUE × gpu_seconds × gpu_watts / 3,600` replaces the token estimate for that event. The default **0.1×–10×** range shows sensitivity to those assumptions. It is not a statistical confidence interval; actual energy may lie outside it. Training, hardware manufacturing, network traffic, your device and unrecorded agent work are outside the estimate. [Methodology and calibration](docs/methodology.md). ## Configuration and privacy The data directory is selected by `--data-dir`, then `AGENTKCAL_HOME`, then `$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentkcal` or `~/.local/share/agentkcal`. `init` creates `config.json` without overwriting an existing file. Configure source paths and model profiles there. Changing energy settings recalculates reports from the original counts without another import. [Configuration reference](docs/configuration.md). SQLite stores usage identifiers, UTC timestamps, model IDs, token counts and optional GPU telemetry. Prompts, responses, tool arguments and credentials are not stored. The dashboard binds to `127.0.0.1`; it is intended for one person's local machine. [Data handling, backups and trust boundaries](docs/privacy.md). ## Documentation - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): released versions, compatibility notes and unreleased changes. - [CLI reference](docs/cli.md): commands, filters, exports and troubleshooting. - [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): data locations, source discovery and energy profiles. - [Agent integrations](docs/integrations.md): Claude status line, MCP and host commands. - [Adapter formats](docs/adapters.md): supported records and deduplication rules. - [Methodology](docs/methodology.md): assumptions, formulas and food values. - [Privacy](docs/privacy.md): stored data, permissions and local access. - [Extension guide](docs/extending.md): TypeScript adapter and provider interfaces. ## Development The application uses TypeScript 7, Node's built-in SQLite and HTTP APIs, and plain HTML/CSS. There are no runtime npm dependencies. Biome handles linting and formatting. ```sh npm ci npm run check npm run typecheck npm test npm run test:package ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for project structure, testing and contribution guidelines. Dependency updates are grouped monthly through Dependabot; major upgrades require manual review. ## Project status AgentKcal **0.1.x is alpha software**. Source formats can change. Imports rescan selected files, and reports load matching events into memory, so large histories can take time and memory. Deleted logs, incomplete counters, compacted histories and forks can affect completeness or create ambiguous identities. See [known accounting limitations](docs/adapters.md#identity-and-completeness). Licensed under [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). [Security policy](SECURITY.md) · [Code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

AgentKcal

Использование AI-агентов в токенах, ватт-часах и привычных продуктах.

AgentKcal объединяет данные об использовании AI-агентов в локальном журнале. Он показывает потреблённые токены, оценивает энергозатраты в ватт-часах и килокалориях по настраиваемому сценарию и сравнивает эту энергию с привычными продуктами. Для ежедневной работы доступны CLI и компактные сводки внутри агентов, для истории и сравнений — локальный dashboard. Записи хранятся в SQLite; само приложение не делает исходящих сетевых запросов. **Энергозатраты рассчитываются по допущениям, а не измеряются.** Килокалории выражают эквивалент той же физической энергии, а не съеденную пищу или калории, потраченные человеком. [Как устроена оценка](docs/methodology.md). [![Dashboard AgentKcal: тестовые данные, оценка энергии, сравнение с продуктами и история агентов](docs/images/dashboard-ru.png)](docs/images/dashboard-ru.png) _Светлая тема и синтетические демоданные. Откройте изображение, чтобы посмотреть скриншот в полном разрешении._ ## Быстрый старт Нужны **Node.js 24.12+** и npm. ```sh git clone https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal.git cd AgentKcal npm ci npm run build npm run demo ``` Откройте **http://127.0.0.1:8765**. Демо использует временную базу, не читает ваши журналы и удаляет свои данные при штатном завершении. Для остановки сервера нажмите **Ctrl+C**. Примеры ниже запускаются прямо из репозитория. CLI также можно [установить из собранного пакета](docs/cli.md#install-the-cli). Готовый архив CLI и контрольная сумма SHA-256 доступны в [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal/releases). [История версий](CHANGELOG.md). ## Учёт своих данных ```sh # Создать конфигурацию и посмотреть доступные адаптеры. node dist/cli.js init node dist/cli.js agents # Импортировать локальные журналы и получить сводку за сегодня по UTC. node dist/cli.js sync node dist/cli.js status --language ru # Посмотреть другой период или открыть dashboard. node dist/cli.js summary --days 30 node dist/cli.js serve ``` Импорт можно повторять: неизменившиеся события пропускаются, обновлённые снимки заменяют существующие записи. Кнопка синхронизации в dashboard выполняет тот же импорт. Обычное обновление страницы читает базу без импорта журналов. Для агентов с экспортами или явно выбранными журналами задач: ```sh node dist/cli.js sync --adapter cursor --path ./cursor-usage.csv node dist/cli.js sync --adapter opencode --path ./session-export.json node dist/cli.js sync --adapter cline --path /path/to/tasks ``` Изолированный пример, который не использует ваш основной журнал: ```sh node dist/cli.js --data-dir ./local-data sync --adapter generic --path examples/usage.jsonl node dist/cli.js --data-dir ./local-data summary --days 0 ``` Все команды, фильтры, форматы экспорта и коды завершения описаны в [справочнике CLI](docs/cli.md). ## Поддерживаемые агенты - **Claude Code:** локальные проектные JSONL, включая вложенные журналы субагентов. Учитывается `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. - **Codex:** rollout JSONL из каталогов сессий и архивных сессий. Учитывается `CODEX_HOME`. - **Gemini CLI:** локальные JSON и JSONL сессий в `~/.gemini/tmp/`. - **Cursor:** Usage CSV с необходимыми колонками счётчиков токенов. - **OpenCode:** JSON-экспорты сессий с классическими или плоскими сообщениями. - **Cline:** явно выбранные журналы задач `ui_messages.json`. - **Другие агенты:** нормализованный JSONL через адаптер `generic` или отдельный TypeScript-адаптер. Поддержка зависит от формата источника и наличия счётчиков. Подключение MCP само по себе не добавляет недостающую телеметрию. [Форматы, стандартные пути и правила учёта](docs/adapters.md). ## Сводки внутри агентов ```sh node dist/cli.js status --agent codex --sync --language ru node dist/cli.js integration --agent claude --language ru node dist/cli.js integration --agent codex ``` - **Claude Code:** постоянная нативная строка состояния показывает токены текущей сессии и приблизительные Wh/ккал без вызова модели. - **Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode и Cline:** локальный stdio MCP-сервер позволяет получать компактные сводки по запросу в диалоге. Для удобного вызова доступны skill и шаблоны команд. Команда `integration` печатает настройки для добавления в конфигурацию агента, не изменяя её. Инструменты MCP разделены: `get_usage` читает сводку, `sync_usage` обновляет источники. Чтение сводки не запускает скрытый импорт. Результат MCP попадает в контекст агента и может передаваться его провайдеру модели. Сама база остаётся локальной. [Настройка интеграций](docs/integrations.md). ## Языки, темы и сравнения с продуктами Dashboard и компактные сводки поддерживают **английский, русский, испанский, немецкий, французский, японский и бразильский португальский**. Языковые коды: `en`, `ru`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `ja`, `pt-BR`. При первом посещении выбирается поддерживаемый язык браузера; изменить его можно в верхней панели. Форматы чисел, дат и названий порций зависят от языка. Идентификаторы агентов и моделей, пользовательские названия сценариев, диагностика источников и поля экспортов сохраняют исходный вид. Общая справка CLI и полные текстовые отчёты доступны на английском. Доступны темы **Системная**, **Светлая** и **Тёмная**. Системная реагирует на изменения оформления ОС. Язык, тема и выбранный продукт сохраняются в localStorage браузера и синхронизируются между вкладками одного локального адреса. Блок сравнения переводит оценку в ккал в условное количество **гречки, пельменей, хлеба, молока, бананов, риса, кукурузы или картофеля**. Для каждого продукта указаны масса порции и её калорийность. Пять иллюстраций показывают целые или частичные порции; дополнительные учитываются в числовой отметке. Полоса показывает долю следующей порции. Это сравнение энергий, а не цель питания и не запись о съеденной пище. [Порции, формулы и источники](docs/methodology.md#food-comparisons). ## Расчёт и точность Адаптеры приводят исходные счётчики к непересекающимся категориям: ```text input + output + cache_read + cache_write + reasoning = total_tokens ``` Для каждой категории задаётся расход Wh на миллион токенов. Сумма умножается на PUE — коэффициент дополнительных энергозатрат дата-центра: ```text Wh = PUE × Σ(токены_категории × Wh_на_миллион / 1 000 000) kcal = Wh × 3 600 / 4 184 ``` Начальные коэффициенты: **100 для входа, 400 для выхода, 10 для чтения кэша, 125 для записи кэша и 400 для размышлений**, при **PUE 1,2**. Это условные допущения для всех моделей, а не измеренные показатели эффективности поставщиков. При переданных времени и мощности GPU формула `PUE × gpu_seconds × gpu_watts / 3 600` заменяет оценку по токенам для того же события. Диапазон **0,1×–10×** показывает чувствительность к допущениям. Это не статистический доверительный интервал; реальный расход может оказаться за его пределами. Обучение, производство оборудования, сеть, ваше устройство и неотражённая работа агентов не учитываются. [Методика и калибровка](docs/methodology.md). ## Конфигурация и приватность Каталог данных выбирается по `--data-dir`, затем `AGENTKCAL_HOME`, затем `$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentkcal` или `~/.local/share/agentkcal`. `init` создаёт `config.json`, не перезаписывая существующий файл. В нём настраиваются пути к источникам и профили моделей. Изменение энергетических параметров пересчитывает отчёты по исходным счётчикам без повторного импорта. [Справочник конфигурации](docs/configuration.md). SQLite хранит идентификаторы записей, время UTC, модели, счётчики токенов и необязательную телеметрию GPU. Промпты, ответы, аргументы инструментов и учётные данные не сохраняются. Dashboard слушает `127.0.0.1` и рассчитан на одного пользователя локального компьютера. [Хранение, резервные копии и границы доступа](docs/privacy.md). ## Документация - [История изменений](CHANGELOG.md): выпущенные версии, совместимость и ещё не выпущенные изменения. - [CLI](docs/cli.md): команды, фильтры, экспорт и решение проблем. - [Конфигурация](docs/configuration.md): каталоги данных, источники и энергетические профили. - [Интеграции](docs/integrations.md): строка состояния Claude, MCP и команды агентов. - [Форматы адаптеров](docs/adapters.md): поддерживаемые записи и устранение дубликатов. - [Методика](docs/methodology.md): допущения, формулы и калорийность продуктов. - [Приватность](docs/privacy.md): сохраняемые данные, права и локальный доступ. - [Расширение проекта](docs/extending.md): интерфейсы адаптеров и провайдеров TypeScript. # Code of conduct

AgentKcal welcomes users and contributors with different experience levels and backgrounds. Discuss technical choices with evidence, explain assumptions and treat other participants respectfully.

## Expected behavior

- Give constructive feedback about code, documentation and ideas.
- Respect different levels of technical experience.
- Keep conversations focused on the issue or contribution.
- Protect other people's privacy, including usage metadata and agent conversations.

Harassment, discriminatory abuse, threats, sexualized content directed at others, and disclosure of another person's private information are not acceptable.

## Reporting and enforcement

Report concerns through a private repository contact channel where available. If no channel is available, request one in an issue without disclosing sensitive information publicly. Security vulnerabilities should follow the [security policy](SECURITY.md).

Maintainers should handle reports discreetly, disclose details only as needed to investigate, and avoid conflicts of interest. Retaliation against a person who reports a concern in good faith is not acceptable. When practical, affected participants should have an opportunity to respond privately.

Maintainers may edit or remove content and restrict participation in response to violations. Enforcement considers the behavior, its impact and the context. Good-faith technical disagreement is welcome.

This policy applies to project issues, pull requests, reviews, discussions and other project interactions.

# Contributing to AgentKcal

Contributions can improve agent-format support, accounting correctness, translations, usability and estimation methodology. For changes to the event contract, data model, runtime dependencies or default energy assumptions, open an issue to discuss the proposed behavior first.

## Set up a development environment

Use Node.js 24.12+ and npm:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal.git
cd AgentKcal
npm ci
npm run build
npm run demo
```

The demo uses temporary synthetic data. For other experiments, select a disposable `--data-dir`; automated tests must not read personal agent logs.

## Project structure

- `src/adapters/`: source discovery and normalization into disjoint token buckets.
- `src/providers/`: energy estimation from normalized usage.
- `src/storage.ts`: SQLite persistence and record identity.
- `src/service.ts`: imports, aggregation, filters and exports.
- `src/integrations/`: compact summaries, host configuration and stdio MCP.
- `src/web/`: dashboard, translations, styles and original SVG assets.
- `integrations/`: distributable skills and command templates.
- `tests/`: Node test-runner tests and synthetic fixtures.
- `scripts/`: asset packaging and installed-package checks.
- `docs/`: user guides and technical references.

CLI, HTTP and MCP share accounting logic. Keep adapters independent of energy coefficients and providers independent of agent file formats. Prefer built-in APIs and existing modules before adding dependencies. [Adapter and provider extension guide](docs/extending.md).

## Checks

```sh
npm run check
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run test:package
```

`check` runs Biome for linting, formatting and import organization. `typecheck` checks server code, browser code and tests. `test` builds dashboard assets and runs the TypeScript suite using Node's test runner. `test:package` packs the application, installs it without development dependencies in a temporary directory, and exercises its CLI, MCP and dashboard.

The root `.editorconfig` defines UTF-8, two-space indentation, a final newline and LF line endings. `.gitattributes` enforces LF in Git checkouts on every platform. Enable EditorConfig support in your editor; Biome remains the formatter and lint authority. Markdown trailing spaces are preserved because they can represent hard line breaks.

Run `npm run format` to apply formatting and safe lint fixes. Integration Markdown templates are kept verbatim to preserve their YAML front matter. CSS rules allow component-specific cascade ordering and documented accessibility exceptions.

CI runs the same checks on Linux, macOS and Windows, including the minimum supported Node.js version on Linux. Dependabot groups dependency updates monthly; review major upgrades separately.

## Tests and fixtures

Add regression tests for behavior that can change totals or data boundaries: bucket semantics, stable identities, streaming snapshots, cumulative counters, malformed files, rollback and privacy. Fixture records must be synthetic or fully redacted. Do not submit prompts, model responses, tool arguments, credentials, account IDs or identifying filesystem paths.

A source-format change should cite its schema or upstream implementation and explain whether cache and reasoning counters overlap other buckets. Verify repeat imports and updates, not just the first import.

For dashboard changes, inspect a populated view and an empty/error state at narrow and wide widths. Check keyboard access, both color themes and long translated labels. Preserve the distinction between estimated energy and measured usage.

Compact CLI/MCP translations live in `src/integrations/languages.ts`. Keep their language codes aligned with the dashboard. Test browser-language detection, saved preferences and representative long labels. Screenshots in the READMEs should use the isolated demo; never capture personal logs.

# Security policy

AgentKcal is designed for one user's local machine. Its dashboard binds to `127.0.0.1`; its MCP server runs over local stdio. The application does not provide a shared hosting or multi-user security model.

## Supported versions

Security fixes target the latest published version in the `0.1.x` line, including alpha releases. Update to the latest available release before reporting a problem with an older version.

Run `agentkcal --version` to identify the installed version. Download packages from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal/releases) and verify their archive against the attached `SHA256SUMS`.

## Report a vulnerability

Use the repository's [private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal/security/advisories/new) when available. If the form is unavailable, open an issue requesting a private contact channel without posting exploit details, secrets or private logs.

Include:
- The affected AgentKcal version, Node.js version and operating system.
- A minimal reproduction using synthetic data.
- The affected interface: CLI import/export, local HTTP dashboard, status line or stdio MCP.
- The expected access boundary and the observed impact.
- Any relevant configuration with personal paths and identifiers removed.

Do not attach real agent histories, credentials or account data. Coordinate disclosure through the private reporting channel.

## Scope

Issues that expose local data, bypass the dashboard's origin protections, execute source-provided commands or access files outside documented interfaces can be security vulnerabilities. Programs already running with access to the same user account are within the local trust boundary.

Energy-estimation accuracy is addressed by the [methodology](docs/methodology.md). Data storage, permissions and MCP context sharing are described in [privacy](docs/privacy.md).

## Problem and behavior

Explain the concrete problem and the resulting behavior. Link the relevant issue if there is one.

## Validation

List the commands run and their results, or explain what could not be checked.
- Adapter/accounting changes: use synthetic fixtures; explain bucket semantics, stable record identity, repeated imports and failure handling.
- Dashboard changes: inspect populated, empty and error states at narrow and wide widths, with both themes and affected languages.
- Packaging/integration changes: run `npm run test:package`.

## Compatibility and documentation

Describe any changes to commands, source formats, configuration, storage or estimation assumptions. Update the relevant guides and add an `Unreleased` changelog entry for user-visible changes. State any known limitations.

Do not include private journals, conversation content, credentials or identifying local paths. Follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md); report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

# Adapter formats

Use `agentkcal agents` to inspect current roots. Defaults are read-only. An explicit `--path` requires `--adapter`; this prevents attempting to parse a file using every adapter. Directories are searched using adapter-specific patterns. Export directories should be dedicated to the relevant format.

## Claude Code

Source: `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`, or `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/`. Includes nested subagents.

Only `type: assistant` entries with `message.usage` are imported. `message.id` plus session identity identifies the record. Last snapshot in a file wins, so streaming chunks are not summed. Cache-read and cache-creation counters are disjoint from input. Output includes thinking if the originating API counts it there; reasoning is not added independently.

Source semantics: [monitoring](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage), [Anthropic caching fields](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/skills/claude-api/shared/prompt-caching.md).

## Codex

Source: `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and `archived_sessions`, with `~/.codex` as the default home.

Reads `session_meta`, model from `turn_context`, and `event_msg` / `token_count` / `info.total_token_usage`. Repeated cumulative snapshots produce no new usage. `last_token_usage` is not summed. Cache read/write are subtracted from total input; reasoning is subtracted from total output to create disjoint buckets. Absent optional cache-write counters are zero. An absent model remains `unknown`.

The first available cumulative snapshot includes all prior usage reflected in that snapshot and is attributed to that timestamp. Decreasing counters and inconsistent subsets reject the file because a reset cannot be distinguished reliably from inconsistent data. Non-rollout event streams, custom app transports, and `token_usage_record` variants are not supported by this adapter.

Source: [Codex protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs). Protocol schemas evolve; attach a minimal redacted fixture when requesting support for a changed format.

## Gemini CLI

Source: `~/.gemini/tmp/**/chats/session-*.json` or `.jsonl`.

JSON snapshots contain `sessionId` and `messages`. JSONL records contain metadata, full messages, optional `$set` metadata updates, and content patches. Full `type: gemini` messages with `tokens` are imported. Repeated messages replace earlier snapshots. Content patches and rewinds do not remove already consumed inference. Legacy `$set.messages` snapshots are accepted.

`input` includes `cached`; subtract cache from input, retain `output` and `thoughts` separately, and add separately reported `tool` prompt tokens to uncached input. Omitted counters default to zero. This follows the recording schema's mapping to API counters; unusual provider counter semantics still require a dedicated fixture.

Sources: [session management](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/cli/session-management.md), [recording types](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingTypes.ts), [API counter mapping](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingService.ts).

## Cursor

Export usage as CSV from your account's Usage dashboard, then import the local file:

```sh
agentkcal sync --adapter cursor --path ./cursor-usage.csv
```

Required case-sensitive columns: `Date`, `Model`, `Input (w/ Cache Write)`, `Input (w/o Cache Write)`, `Cache Read`, `Output Tokens`. Dates require an ISO 8601 timezone offset or `Z`. Counts must be integers; quoted counts containing thousands separators are accepted. UTF-8 BOM is accepted. Other columns are ignored for totals. Included/subscription usage counts too, because token consumption is independent of the row's price. Rows lacking counters fail rather than turning missing usage into zero.

No cloud API, authentication or editor database integration is included. CSV schemas vary by account and product release; unsupported schemas are rejected. User identity, where present, participates only in an in-memory identity hash and is not stored as a separate field.

## OpenCode

Import a local session JSON export with `info.id` and a `messages` array:

```sh
agentkcal sync --adapter opencode --path ./session-export.json
```

Classic message shape: `{ "info": { "id", "role": "assistant", "modelID", "time", "tokens" }, "parts": [] }`. Newer flat messages use `type: assistant`, `model`, `time`, and `tokens` directly. Usage-bearing compaction records are also accepted. Model reference uses `modelID` or `id` where present, otherwise `unknown`. Time is a millisecond epoch value or an ISO timestamp with offset. Buckets `input`, `output`, `reasoning`, `cache.read`, `cache.write` are disjoint. Exported session aggregate totals are not added to per-message counters.

Use your installed OpenCode version's session export command. Sources: [export handler](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/session/export.ts), [transfer schema](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/schema/src/session-transfer.ts), [usage normalization](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/session/usage.ts). Native database schemas are not accessed.

## Cline

Explicitly select a task's `ui_messages.json` or a tasks directory. The JSON must be an array of Cline messages. Usage-bearing `say` records of kind `api_req_started` and `subagent_usage` contain JSON text with `tokensIn`, `tokensOut`, `cacheReads`, and `cacheWrites`. Record `ts` is a millisecond epoch timestamp and an identity within the task directory's name. Request text is ignored and never persisted. Finished messages are not counted again.

`deleted_api_reqs` aggregates are excluded because they overlap previously imported requests and lack individual stable identities. A first import after compaction can undercount deleted history. The ledger retains previously imported records even if source history is later pruned. Model is `unknown`, so configure a fallback energy scenario accordingly. Renaming a task directory changes its inferred session identity; do not reimport renamed copies into the same ledger.

Source: [Cline metrics](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/apps/vscode/src/shared/getApiMetrics.ts), [message types](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/apps/vscode/src/shared/ExtensionMessage.ts).

## Universal JSONL

One normalized `UsageEvent` per line. Required: `agent`, `event_id`, `session_id`, `timestamp`. Optional: `model` (defaults to `unknown`), all five token buckets (default zero), `gpu_seconds` and `gpu_watts` (supply together). Unknown fields are rejected; do not include prompts or secrets. ISO timestamps require timezone offsets; numeric timestamps, if used, are milliseconds. See [example](../examples/usage.jsonl).

Agent, event, session and model IDs must be non-empty strings up to 512 characters. Token counts must be finite non-negative integers. GPU telemetry must be finite, non-negative, and paired. Reuse stable event/session IDs to update a record rather than inserting another copy. Do not import both native and generic copies of the same work under different identities.

## Identity and completeness

- Ledger key: `(agent, session_id, event_id)`. Reimporting unchanged records is a no-op; later snapshots update existing records.
- A whole file is parsed under the SQLite writer lock before the transaction writes its normalized events. Concurrent imports wait for that lock before reading the source. Malformed or truncated files commit no partial prefix; retry when their writer finishes. Other valid files continue importing, including when a discovered file is missing or unreadable.
- Default roots that do not exist are normal for uninstalled agents. Missing explicit paths produce warnings; empty or unsupported files also produce warnings.
- The ledger is append/update oriented. Removing source logs does not remove usage. There is no automatic pruning or source-snapshot reconciliation.
- CSV exports have no reliable native request ID. AgentKcal hashes usage identity and user identity, plus an occurrence ordinal for otherwise identical rows. Repeated copies of the same export deduplicate. Overlapping exports can be ambiguous when identical rows represent distinct requests, or metadata/counters change. Cursor's `session_id` is the placeholder `cursor-csv`; it is not a real session count.
- Mirrored or forked histories with different session IDs can double-count shared ancestry. AgentKcal does not reconcile across identities, devices, native/generic imports, or vendors.
- Counts reflect available data, not a claim of complete account usage. Private backend work, deleted logs, dropped counters, and some compaction/retry records can be absent.
- Every sync rescans selected sources and materializes each file's normalized events before writing. Very large histories can consume substantial memory and time. Reports also materialize matching ledger events.

The formats described above define supported inputs. Upstream schemas can change; include a minimal synthetic record and the agent version when reporting an unsupported format.

# CLI reference

Run commands from a built repository with `node dist/cli.js`. After installing the package, use `agentkcal` instead.

```sh
node dist/cli.js --help
node dist/cli.js --version
```

## Install the CLI

Download `agentkcal-0.1.0.tgz` and `SHA256SUMS` from the [v0.1.0 alpha release](https://github.com/0then0/AgentKcal/releases/tag/v0.1.0) into the same directory. Verify the archive before installing:

macOS:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
```

Linux:

```sh
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

Windows PowerShell: compare the resulting hash with the matching entry in `SHA256SUMS`.

```powershell
Get-FileHash ./agentkcal-0.1.0.tgz -Algorithm SHA256
```

Then install the compiled package:

```sh
npm install --global ./agentkcal-0.1.0.tgz
agentkcal --version
agentkcal demo
```

The package is distributed through GitHub release assets. No npm registry installation is required. Use the asset name for the version you download; see [release history](../CHANGELOG.md).

To build a package from the repository instead:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm pack
npm install --global ./agentkcal-0.1.0.tgz
```

The archive contains compiled code and dashboard assets. The installed CLI requires Node.js 24.12+; it does not need development dependencies. When installing a different version, use the archive name printed by `npm pack`.

To remove the global installation:

```sh
npm uninstall --global agentkcal
```

This removes the executable, not your usage database. [Manage local data](privacy.md#back-up-or-remove-data).

## Data directory

Set `--data-dir PATH` to keep an experiment or another workspace separate:

```sh
node dist/cli.js --data-dir ./local-data status
```

Without the flag, AgentKcal uses `AGENTKCAL_HOME`, then `$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentkcal`, or `~/.local/share/agentkcal`. See [configuration](configuration.md#data-directory).

## Initialize and inspect

```sh
node dist/cli.js init
node dist/cli.js agents
```

`init` creates the default `config.json` if it is missing and prints its path. Existing configuration is preserved.

`agents` prints JSON with each adapter's ID, title, mode, configured paths and whether any source root exists. A found directory does not necessarily contain supported usage records. This command is useful when a sync finds no data.

## Import usage

```sh
node dist/cli.js sync
node dist/cli.js sync --adapter claude
node dist/cli.js sync --adapter cursor --path ./cursor-usage.csv
node dist/cli.js sync --adapter generic --path ./first.jsonl --path ./second.jsonl
```

Without `--adapter`, sync checks every adapter's default or configured roots. `--path` selects files or directories for this invocation and requires `--adapter`; it does not save paths to the configuration. Repeat `--path` to select multiple locations.

The JSON result contains:
- `files`: files examined.
- `records`: normalized records read from successful files, including unchanged records.
- `changed`: records inserted or updated in SQLite.
- `errors` and `warnings`: per-source diagnostics.

A valid file imports in one transaction. A malformed or truncated file is skipped in full, while other files continue. Unchanged records are not duplicated. Source formats and identity rules are documented in [adapters](adapters.md).

## Compact status

```sh
node dist/cli.js status
node dist/cli.js status --days 7 --agent codex
node dist/cli.js status --agent claude --session SESSION_ID --days 0
node dist/cli.js status --sync --agent codex --language ru
node dist/cli.js status --days 0 --json
```

`status` defaults to today in UTC and reads the existing ledger. Use `--sync` to refresh configured sources before displaying it. `--agent` filters by a normalized agent ID; when combined with `--sync`, that ID must also be a registered adapter.

Supported periods are `1`, `7`, `30`, `90`, or `0` for all time. `--session` filters by a known native session ID. Cursor CSV records use the shared placeholder `cursor-csv`, not real session IDs.

`--language` accepts `en`, `ru`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `ja` and `pt-BR`. JSON output includes totals, the selected filters, the read timestamp, the last matching event's timestamp and the scenario label. The read timestamp alone does not indicate when source files were last imported.

## Full summary

```sh
node dist/cli.js summary --days 30
node dist/cli.js summary --days 0 --agent codex --json
```

`summary` defaults to 30 days. Supported periods are `7`, `30`, `90`, or `0`. Text output shows totals and the agent breakdown. JSON also includes per-model totals, daily values, matching records and the complete energy scenario.

All periods use UTC calendar days including today. Future-dated events are omitted until their timestamps are reached. Empty days are included in fixed-length daily series. A summary reads the ledger without refreshing logs.

## Export

```sh
node dist/cli.js export --days 30 --format json --output usage.json
node dist/cli.js export --days 0 --agent codex --format csv --output usage.csv
node dist/cli.js export --days 7 --format json
```

Without `--output`, export writes to stdout. A file is created exclusively: an existing destination is never overwritten. Supported formats are `json` (default) and `csv`; periods and agent filtering match `summary`.

JSON includes the normalized records, totals and exact scenario configuration. CSV includes a JSON-valued `scenario` column on each row. Text fields beginning with spreadsheet formula markers receive a leading apostrophe. Exports contain every matching record, while the dashboard's recent-usage table shows at most 100.

Exported identifiers and model names can still contain identifying metadata. Treat the resulting files as private usage records.

## Dashboard and demo

```sh
node dist/cli.js serve
node dist/cli.js --data-dir ./local-data serve --port 8766
node dist/cli.js demo --port 8767
```

Both commands bind to IPv4 `127.0.0.1`. Open the exact URL printed by the CLI. The default port is `8765`; `--port 0` requests a free port. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

`serve` uses the selected data directory. `demo` uses a separate temporary ledger with synthetic data and disables log sync. Its temporary files are removed on normal shutdown.

## Agent integration commands

```sh
node dist/cli.js integration --agent claude --language ru
node dist/cli.js integration --agent codex
node dist/cli.js mcp
```

`integration` prints configuration for `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `cline` or generic `mcp`. It never edits host settings. `--language` controls the generated Claude status line.

`mcp` runs the local stdio server. Its stdout is reserved for newline-delimited MCP messages, so start it through an MCP host rather than using it as an interactive summary command.

`statusline --language CODE` is the native Claude entry point. Claude supplies JSON on stdin with `session_id` and `transcript_path`; malformed or temporarily incomplete input produces a short unavailable message. [Integration setup](integrations.md).

## Exit codes and troubleshooting

- `0`: the command succeeded. The Claude status-line entry point also uses 0 for its waiting/unavailable display states.
- `1`: invalid arguments, configuration/storage errors, or any warning/error during an explicit sync. Successful files from that sync remain imported.

For **no data**, run `agents`, check source paths, import the appropriate export, and use `--days 0` for older history. A newly connected MCP host still needs its sources configured and imported.

For a **malformed or truncated source**, retry after the agent finishes writing. The skipped file does not partially import.

For an **invalid configuration**, check the JSON and required settings in [configuration](configuration.md). Values must be finite numbers, and the final model profile must be `*`.

For an **occupied port**, stop the other local server or choose another `--port`. A port change creates a different browser origin, so browser preferences may differ.

# Configuration reference

AgentKcal stores source settings and energy coefficients in `config.json` inside its data directory. Create the file with `node dist/cli.js init`, then edit it with a text editor. Configuration is read when a command or dashboard request needs it.

## Data directory

Location priority:
1. `--data-dir PATH`.
2. `AGENTKCAL_HOME`.
3. `$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentkcal`, or `~/.local/share/agentkcal` when `XDG_DATA_HOME` is unset.

Use an absolute path when the CLI and an agent integration must share the same ledger. Relative paths resolve from the process's working directory. Tilde expansion is supported for `~` and `~/...`.

The directory contains `config.json`, `usage.sqlite3` and SQLite's associated write-ahead log/shared-memory files. Browser language, theme and food preferences are stored separately in localStorage.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sources": {},
  "energy": {
    "label": "Illustrative scenario · not a measurement",
    "pue": 1.2,
    "low_multiplier": 0.1,
    "high_multiplier": 10,
    "profiles": [
      {
        "model_pattern": "*",
        "input_wh_per_million": 100,
        "output_wh_per_million": 400,
        "cache_read_wh_per_million": 10,
        "cache_write_wh_per_million": 125,
        "reasoning_wh_per_million": 400
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`version` must be `1`. Initialization preserves an existing file. If configuration is invalid, the command reports an error instead of silently applying different coefficients.

## Sources

`sources` maps adapter IDs to lists of file or directory paths. For example, add these entries when the files exist:

```json
{
  "cursor": ["~/Downloads/cursor-usage.csv"],
  "opencode": ["~/exports/opencode"],
  "cline": ["/path/to/tasks"]
}
```

This object is the value of `sources` in the full configuration.
- An omitted adapter uses its default roots.
- A configured list replaces that adapter's defaults.
- An empty list disables discovery for that adapter.
- Paths support `~`, files and directories, but not shell variables or glob expressions.
- Unknown adapter IDs are reported during sync.

Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI have default local roots. Cursor, OpenCode, Cline and generic imports require explicit paths. See [adapter formats](adapters.md) for each directory pattern and supported file shape.

To select a path for just one import, use `sync --adapter ID --path PATH`. This does not change `sources`.

## Energy settings

`label` is a non-empty description of the scenario. It appears in the dashboard and exports; custom labels are kept in their original language. Include the basis of your coefficients so exported results remain interpretable.

`pue` is the data-center overhead multiplier and must be at least `1`. Set it to `1` if the supplied coefficients or power values already include facility overhead.

`low_multiplier` is between `0` and `1`. `high_multiplier` is at least `1`. They scale the central estimate to form a sensitivity range, including events estimated from GPU telemetry. The range is not a measured error bound or confidence interval.

All numeric settings must be finite. Boolean values and numeric strings are rejected.

## Model profiles

Profiles are tested in order. Matching uses case-insensitive glob patterns (`*`, `?` and character classes); the first match wins. The last profile must use `model_pattern: "*"` so every model has a fallback.

Each profile requires five non-negative coefficients, in Wh per million tokens:
- `input_wh_per_million`: uncached input.
- `output_wh_per_million`: output excluding separately reported reasoning.
- `cache_read_wh_per_million`: cached input reads.
- `cache_write_wh_per_million`: cache creation/write tokens.
- `reasoning_wh_per_million`: separately reported reasoning.

Copy the fallback profile, change its pattern and coefficients, and place it before `*`. Values should describe your chosen system boundary and evidence. A model name alone does not determine hardware, batching or energy consumption. [Calibration guidance](methodology.md#calibrate-a-scenario).

Changing a profile recalculates reports from the existing token counts; another import is not required. Refresh the dashboard or change a filter to read saved changes. JSON exports include the full scenario, allowing an exported estimate to be interpreted after the configuration changes.

## Storage compatibility

The ledger uses SQLite schema version `1` and identifies records by `(agent, session_id, event_id)`. Existing version-1 ledgers are read in place. A newer, unsupported schema version is rejected rather than migrated automatically.

Keep a backup before replacing or moving a data directory. [Backup and removal](privacy.md#back-up-or-remove-data).

# In-agent usage

The everyday view is a compact line of tokens, approximate Wh and kcal. The dashboard remains the place for history, breakdowns and food comparisons. All integrations use the same normalized ledger and energy provider. They do not convert API prices or subscription limits into energy.

## A compact command

After building the checkout, use `node dist/cli.js` in place of `agentkcal`, or install the local npm package as described in the README.

```sh
agentkcal status --language ru
agentkcal status --agent codex --days 7
agentkcal status --agent codex --sync --language ru
agentkcal status --agent claude --session SESSION_ID --days 0 --json
```

Supported `--language` codes are `en`, `ru`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `ja` and `pt-BR`; the same values are accepted by MCP `get_usage`.

The default is **today's UTC calendar date**, across agents. `--days 0` means all time. `--session` requires a known native session ID; AgentKcal does not guess it. `status` reads the ledger; `--sync` explicitly refreshes configured logs first and returns status 1 if any import warns or fails. JSON includes the last recorded event timestamp, the read timestamp, scenario label and uncertainty range. Empty usage is zero, while very small positive estimates display `<0.01`.

## Claude Code: persistent native status line

Run:

```sh
agentkcal integration --agent claude --language ru
```

Merge the printed `statusLine` property into `~/.claude/settings.json` (or project settings). Review an existing status line before replacing it; compose commands manually if you already use one. The generator prints configuration only and never edits another application's files.

Claude passes `session_id` and `transcript_path` on stdin. AgentKcal reads that transcript with the Claude adapter, imports its normalized records idempotently, and displays **that session's** tokens and estimated Wh/kcal. It does not scan all agents or treat context-window occupancy as cumulative consumption. Native stdin metadata, prompts and responses are not stored. The command renders a short waiting/unavailable message when a transcript is missing, incomplete or invalid; no private parser diagnostic appears in the footer. Once data is valid, the next invocation refreshes it.

This path does not invoke a model. It rereads the transcript on each native refresh, so very large sessions can make it slower. It includes only records in that transcript; separate subagent journals appear after normal sync, and are not silently attributed to the main session. Generated settings reference the absolute Node executable, installed CLI and selected data directory. Regenerate after moving the package or Node installation. The command needs filesystem permissions to read the transcript and write the local ledger.

[Claude statusLine documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline).

# Methodology

AgentKcal separates recorded token accounting from an energy scenario. Tokens are reported by software, not verified by a power meter. Their availability and meaning depend on the originating provider and agent version.

## Units and boundaries

One watt-hour is 3,600 joules. One thermochemical kilocalorie is 4,184 joules, so 1 Wh is approximately 0.86042 kcal. This conversion is physical and exact for those unit definitions; the uncertainty is in the energy estimate upstream. Food labels and human metabolism are not part of the model.

The token scenario assigns separate Wh per million tokens to uncached input, visible output, cache reads, cache writes, and separately reported reasoning. The default values are deliberately labeled illustrative. They are not inferred from money spent, model parameters, subscription tier, or a claim about any vendor's efficiency. The default cache relationship is an assumption, not a measured energy saving.

PUE (power usage effectiveness) multiplies the IT energy scenario by a data-center overhead factor. It must be at least 1. The default 1.2 is an assumption, not the PUE of your provider. CPU, memory, storage and host overhead are not separately modeled; calibrate coefficients to your chosen system boundary. Do not apply PUE again if supplied power or coefficients already include facility overhead.

## Calibrate a scenario

Run `agentkcal init` and edit `config.json`. Every profile needs `model_pattern` and all five non-negative finite coefficients:

```json
{
  "model_pattern": "my-local-model*",
  "input_wh_per_million": 100,
  "output_wh_per_million": 400,
  "cache_read_wh_per_million": 10,
  "cache_write_wh_per_million": 125,
  "reasoning_wh_per_million": 400
}
```

These sample values are the same illustrative defaults, not a new benchmark. Insert a profile before the final `*` profile, replace values using your own evidence, and describe that evidence in `energy.label`. First matching model pattern wins. Matching is case-insensitive. Cline may have model `unknown`, so it generally uses the fallback. A model ID alone cannot reveal hardware, quantization, speculative decoding, context length, routing or request batching.

Energy is recalculated from raw normalized records when a report is requested. Export JSON to preserve a result together with the full configuration and generation time; there is no historical configuration version ledger. CSV includes the scenario as a JSON-valued column.

## Compute telemetry

Normalized JSONL can supply both `gpu_seconds` and `gpu_watts`. This selects the compute method for that event, even when token counts are also present:

```text
GPU time: 60 seconds
Effective GPU power: 180 W
PUE: 1.2
Energy: 60 × 180 / 3,600 × 1.2 = 3.6 Wh
Equivalent: 3.6 × 3,600 / 4,184 ≈ 3.0975 kcal
```

GPU time should represent allocated device time summed across the devices attributable to the record. Power should represent the corresponding effective average watts per allocated GPU. A 10-second request is not necessarily 10 GPU-seconds; asynchronous work, shared batching, CPU steps and network waits prevent that equivalence. AgentKcal does not collect hardware telemetry or obtain backend allocation data itself.

## Sensitivity range

The report multiplies the central scenario by `low_multiplier` and `high_multiplier`. Defaults are 0.1 and 10. These are sensitivity controls; no underlying probability distribution or measured coverage supports them. They are not an assurance that the real value is within the range. They apply to supplied-compute scenarios too, because effective power attribution can also be uncertain.

When all profiles produce zero energy, the application reports zero rather than inventing a minimum. Display rounding can turn tiny positive values into `0`; JSON exports retain full numerical precision.

## Completeness

Reported tokens omit work an agent or provider did not record. Private reasoning may be reported separately, inside output, or not at all. Agent retries, compaction, tool calls and subagents are included only where their records are available. Forked transcripts can repeat ancestry. The initial Codex cumulative snapshot is attributed to its recorded time because finer-grained timing is unavailable. Token buckets do not represent unique text, and different tokenizers prevent strict comparison of equivalent work.

The estimate excludes training, embodied hardware energy, agent-host energy, external tool execution, network traffic and user-device consumption. It also does not estimate emissions: converting energy into CO₂ requires additional location/time-dependent evidence. Food comparisons below illustrate equivalent energy; they do not infer actual food consumption, human effort or metabolism.

## Food comparisons

The dashboard uses the same filtered report's kcal and divides by the energy in an explicitly defined comparison portion:

```text
portion_kcal = portion_grams × kcal_per_100g / 100
equivalent_portions = estimated_kcal / portion_kcal
```

Low/high scenario values are converted using the same portion. Nutritional variation is not assigned an additional statistical range. Portion masses are application assumptions, not a claim that every item or package has that size. The comparison catalog uses these reference values:
- **Buckwheat:** an assumed 800 g pack of dry grain, at 335 kcal per 100 g, gives 2,680 kcal per comparison pack. The energy density is listed for Mistral grain by [this retailer](https://www.delo.spb.ru/catalog/product/12092-krupa-grechka-mistral-yadrica-900-g/); its actual retail package is 900 g. AgentKcal deliberately uses a generic assumed 800 g portion. Cooking adds water and changes calories per 100 g, so cooked-porridge mass is not interchangeable with this dry-grain mass.
- **Dumplings:** an assumed 15 g frozen dumpling, at 270 kcal per 100 g, gives 40.5 kcal each. The energy density follows [Sibirskaya Collection's classic product label](https://sibircollection.ru/products/pelmeni/gourmet/klassicheskie/). The weight of one dumpling is an assumption; sauces and preparation are excluded.
- **White bread:** an assumed 400 g loaf, at 265 kcal per 100 g, gives 1,060 kcal. This [retail product listing](https://m.integration.vs.market.yandex.net/card/baton-nareznoy-kolomenskiy-v-narezke/103809380196) reports both values for a sliced white loaf. Other recipes and loaf sizes vary.
- **Milk:** an assumed 1,000 g carton of 3.2% milk, at 59 kcal per 100 g, gives 590 kcal. The energy density comes from [Prostokvashino's product page](https://prostokvashino.ru/product/moloko-pasterizovannoe-3-2--1-4-l/). The comparison uses **mass, not litres**; the manufacturer's listed package has a different volume. No density conversion is assumed.
- **Banana:** an assumed 118 g edible portion without peel, at 89 kcal per 100 g, gives 105.02 kcal. [USDA FoodData Central record 173944](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/173944/nutrients) identifies raw bananas; this [record summary](https://whatyoueat.io/foods/173944-bananas) reports the per-100 g energy. The actual fruit's edible mass varies.

- **Rice:** an assumed 800 g pack of dry white long-grain rice, at 365 kcal per 100 g, gives 2,920 kcal. The per-100 g value is reported in this [USDA-derived record summary](https://nutritiondatahub.com/food/rice-white-long-grain-regular-raw-enriched-168877). The portion is dry grain; cooked rice includes added water and has a different energy density.
- **Corn:** an assumed cob with 100 g of edible raw sweet-corn kernels, at 86 kcal per 100 g, gives 86 kcal. The energy density is reported in this [USDA-derived record summary](https://rawpawiq.com/ingredient/corn-sweet-yellow-raw-169998). Husk and inedible cob mass are excluded; the 100 g edible yield per cob is an application assumption. Canned corn and corn cooked with additions are not this comparison.
- **Potato:** an assumed 150 g raw potato including skin, at 77 kcal per 100 g, gives 115.5 kcal. This [USDA-derived record summary](https://nutritiondatahub.com/food/potatoes-flesh-and-skin-raw-170026) reports the energy density. The assumed tuber mass varies in practice; frying, added oil and other preparations are not modeled.

The panel uses original, unbranded local SVG illustrations and makes no runtime request to food databases or retailers. There is no endorsement, product inventory, personal dietary target or nutrition recommendation. Food definitions live in `src/web/foods.ts`; the UI supports English, Russian, Spanish, German, French, Japanese and Brazilian Portuguese in both themes. Selection is a local browser preference and does not change the underlying ledger or exports.

At most five portion icons are drawn; a badge displays equivalents beyond those five. A partially filled icon represents a fractional portion. The progress bar is `100 × fractional_part(equivalent_portions)` and resets to zero at whole portions, including zero. Quantities are approximately displayed to two decimals, with a less-than label for tiny positive values; unit grammar follows the displayed number. Binary floating-point artifacts at exact whole-portion boundaries are normalized.

- [OpenAI Codex usage protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs): source accounting fields, not energy coefficients.

# Local data and privacy

The app has no telemetry, vendor API clients, remote font, CDN dependency or outbound HTTP request. A normal run reads selected local source files and writes local SQLite and configuration files. Browser requests go to `127.0.0.1`. Shields.io images appear only in the GitHub README, not in the running application.

The database stores agent, session, event and model IDs; UTC timestamps; five normalized token counts; and optional GPU time/power values. Reports derive energy on demand. Prompts, responses, tool arguments, source file contents, raw usernames and credentials are not stored. IDs and model names can still be identifying metadata. Generic imports trust you to choose suitable IDs; do not put secrets or personal text in these fields.

Adapters may parse files containing conversations in memory to extract accounting. These files are never copied wholesale. Diagnostic messages can include local paths or file names and validation messages, but should not include source record bodies. `config.json` contains source paths you configure. CLI `agents` prints the source locations; the dashboard status API omits paths.

## Local files

Dashboard language, theme and comparison-product preferences use the browser's localStorage keys `agentkcal.language`, `agentkcal.theme` and `agentkcal.food` for the current local origin. Only these preferences are stored there; usage remains in SQLite. Preferences are shared between tabs of the same origin and fall back to the current page session if storage is unavailable. Clearing browser storage removes these settings without deleting the usage ledger.

Default directory: `~/.local/share/agentkcal`, with overrides documented in the README. Files include `config.json`, `usage.sqlite3`, and temporary SQLite WAL/SHM files. The database and new configuration/CLI export files are set to mode 0600 where supported; newly created data directories request 0700. Existing parent permissions are not changed. Windows uses its platform ACL behavior. Storage is not encrypted and there is no app-level login.

## Back up or remove data

Treat exports and backups as usage metadata. Stop all writers, including the dashboard, CLI imports and agent integrations, before copying the data directory, or use SQLite's backup tooling. Do not commit local data or raw agent journals. The repository ignores known local data paths, databases and conventional usage export names.

To remove AgentKcal's history, stop all writers and delete its configured data directory yourself after backing up anything needed. This does not remove original agent logs.

## Local server boundary

The dashboard binds only to IPv4 `127.0.0.1` and accepts the exact printed host and port. Cross-origin and cross-site requests are rejected. A per-process token is required for sync. Static assets are served from an explicit allowlist, with a restrictive content security policy and no CORS opt-in. The server does not expose an API for choosing arbitrary import paths; configure those locally or use the CLI.

These controls protect normal browser access, including DNS-rebinding attempts. They do not isolate the app from programs or other users able to access your local account or filesystem. Do not publish the server through a reverse proxy or tunnel and do not use it as a shared hosted service. Running under the same OS user is within the trust boundary.

Demo mode uses a separate temporary directory and disables sync. It does not read agent log contents. Normal shutdown removes the temporary ledger; a forced process termination or machine crash can leave a temporary directory for OS cleanup.

## In-agent summaries

Claude's native statusLine reads only the host-supplied transcript and records normalized usage in the same ledger. Its input metadata is not persisted. The local stdio MCP exposes a compact read tool and a separate configured-source refresh tool; it accepts no paths or executable commands. MCP diagnostics expose counts rather than private source paths. Summary metadata returned to an agent becomes part of its context and may reach its model provider. See [integration boundaries](integrations.md).
